items.descriptionTR: The UK's Prime Minister Keir Starmer has insisted he will fight to stay in his role if a leadership challenge is launched by Andy Burnham. But before any such contest unfolds, Burnham must win a seat in parliament, which he is hoping to do on June 18 in a by-election in the Makerfield constituency. The race is expected to be tight, with Reform UK candidate Rob Kenyon posing a credible opposition to the former Greater Manchester Mayor.
items.titleTR: Starmer rival seeks win in UK by-election pivotal to prime minister's fate

items.descriptionTR: Israel's foreign minister says he is severing contact with the EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas. Gideon Saar attributed the move to a media report alleging that Kallas compared Israel to apartheid-era South Africa.
items.titleTR: Israel says it's cutting ties to EU's Kaja Kallas

slots.packetSpot: Israel's foreign minister announced the severing of contact with EU's Kaja Kallas following reports of her alleged apartheid comparison.

items.descriptionTR: G7 leaders agreed on June 16 to intensify pressure on Russia to end more than four years of war against Ukraine, with US President Donald Trump saying Moscow should "make a deal" and indicating Washington could re-impose waived sanctions. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky joined the summit at the French resort of Evian, hoping that with a deal between the US and Iran ostensibly in the works, the Trump administration will now turn its attention to solving Europe's largest armed conflict since World War II.
items.titleTR: US signals to return of sanctions on Russia as G7 unites around Ukraine

slots.packetSpot: G7 leaders have expressed strong support for Ukraine, discussing measures to strengthen its defense and considering renewed sanctions on Russia. Concurrently, diplomatic engagements involving Putin and other global leaders continue.
slots.packetTitle: G7's Unified Support for Ukraine and Diplomatic Engagements with Russia

items.descriptionTR:
British prime minister was left making small talk unsure if a meeting with Trump and Zelenskyy was going ahead
The wait for Keir Starmer’s first session of the G7 gathering in Évian-les-Bains was undoubtedly awkward. A meeting about the future of Ukraine had been due to start at 9am but more than half an hour later, Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Emmanuel Macron were nowhere to be seen.
On a live Reuters feed, Starmer could be seen standing next to the leaders of Canada and Japan as they milled about making small talk. “Are they, are they having a meeting?” the British prime minister could be heard asking. If he was referring to the missing attenders, and they were indeed having a meeting, it was clear he hadn’t been invited.
items.titleTR: Starmer’s waning influence is apparent at awkward G7 summit

items.titleTR: EU proposes entry ban for Russians who fought in Ukraine

items.descriptionTR:
Kyiv says attack, which also forced evacuation at Russia’s biggest airport, was in response to strike on historic monastery
	•	Explainer: how significant was attack on Moscow?
Ukrainian drones have hit several locations across Moscow in Kyiv’s biggest air raid on the city since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion, setting a major ⁠oil refinery on fire and forcing evacuations at the country’s largest airport.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as a response to Russia’s strike on a historic Kyiv monastery complex earlier this week.
items.titleTR: Moscow oil refinery struck in Ukraine’s biggest air raid on city since start of war

slots.packetSpot: A large-scale Ukrainian drone attack targeted Moscow, setting a major oil refinery on fire and causing disruptions in the city.
slots.packetTitle: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sets Moscow Oil Refinery Ablaze

items.descriptionTR:
US defence secretary addresses allies in latest attempt to get Europe to raise military budgets
Pete Hegseth has announced a review of the US military presence across Europe, in a combative address to Nato allies where he threatened to cut force numbers in countries spending the least on defence.
The US defence secretary, speaking at a meeting of Nato defence ministers in Brussels, accused some countries of “free riding” and others of being shameful for not allowing their airbases to be used by US jets bombing Iran in the spring.
items.titleTR: Pete Hegseth accuses Nato countries of ‘free riding’ in combative address

slots.packetSpot: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has announced a review of the US military presence in Europe, criticizing NATO allies for insufficient defense spending. This move signals a shift in US commitments to NATO's high readiness force.
slots.packetTitle: US Reviews NATO Military Presence Amid Criticism of European Defense Spending

items.descriptionTR:
Keir Starmer has called the firing of warning shots by a Russian warship at a British yacht sailing across the Channel on Tuesday ‘deeply concerning and reckless’.

Russia’s defence ministry said the yacht was on a ‘dangerous course’ and several attempts were made to contact it – a claim disputed by the retired couple onboard the 40ft yacht.

Nosheen Iqbal speaks to the Guardian’s defence and security editor, Dan Sabbagh
items.titleTR: Why did Russian warship fire warning shots in the Channel? – The Latest

items.descriptionTR: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Wednesday that the fatal shooting of exiled Russian artist Semyon Skrepetsky was likely a political assassination. The Kremlin critic, known for provocative caricatures of President Vladimir Putin and other political figures, was shot dead by an unidentified gunman in eastern Poland on Monday.

items.descriptionTR: A main topic of discussion among European leaders at the G7 summit has to do with decreasing the global reliance on the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s success in shuttering the critical waterway has sparked fears that Tehran could use it as an ongoing bargaining chip if a ceasefire and peace deal falls apart. European leaders have pledged military assets to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
